prompt:
Edit the supplied research diagram. Preserve its exact agent/controller/tool feedback topology and persistent-state structure, while improving aesthetics and explicitly labeling the actual models. This is a CVPR paper method figure, NOT a marketing infographic.
Style: polished vector-like scientific systems diagram on pure white, very wide landscape. Fine consistent dark-slate strokes, carefully aligned edges, large legible typography, generous but efficient whitespace. Add restrained pastel header fills: lavender for the composer, pale teal for the controller, pale amber for deterministic tools, blue-gray for memory. Use subtly rounded corners only on major modules, square data tables. No gradients, drop shadows, glossy rendering, cartoons, human silhouettes, clip-art icons, logos, giant title, or decorative banners. The previous monochrome figure was too plain; improve hierarchy and color balance without clutter.
TOP: replace the four plain shared-evidence cells with four equal model-labeled evidence modules. Each has a bold model/tool name and a concise output:
1 "Beat This!" / "2–4-bar windows"
2 "Local choreography expert" / "SFT Qwen3-Omni" / "or MOSS-Music-8B" / small note "one backend per run"
3 "MuQ + style head" / "Global dance-style prior"
4 "librosa" / "RMS · onset · chroma"
Above these four modules add a small source label "Music waveform". Connect it through a shared thin distribution line to the evidence modules, making clear the experts analyze source audio in parallel. Below them a clean shared lane "Frozen evidence and candidate cache" leads DOWN into the controller as read-only context. These are shared tools, not four sequential steps. Do not draw an arrow from the composer to raw audio.
CENTER: retain the dashed "Compositional harness" boundary. The left major module must be clearly labeled "Composer" and show its actual model on two lines "Qwen3-VL" and "30B-A3B-Instruct", with a small "frozen during planning" note. Keep "Outline + motif goals" and "Unit drafts / revisions" as its functions.
Center major module "Controller": "Schedule next stage", "Budget + permissions", "Stop / continue / complete".
Right major module "Tool execution": use actual operation names "read_evidence / read_history", "check_block", "commit_block", and a final ordinary-text row "Repeat scan + text patch". Visually distinguish learned model boxes from deterministic tools using their header colors and simple text labels, not logos.
Preserve EXACT arrow directions: controller → composer labeled "context + feedback"; composer → controller labeled "structured proposal"; controller → tool execution labeled "execute"; tool execution → controller labeled "observation / error". All arrowheads clear and no label overlaps.
BOTTOM inside boundary: persistent state with four compartments "Outline + motif memory", "Current unit draft", "Committed history", "Call / token ledger". Preserve bidirectional read/write arrows between state and controller/tools. Keep one unobtrusive note "Targeted revision uses remaining budget". A small footer says "Evidence binding · protected regions · decision logs".
RIGHT outside boundary: output "Timed choreography text", with a clearly connected arrow FROM the tool execution module, labeled "complete score". Put a tiny example header "Dance style is …" inside output if space permits.
Constraints: all output is TEXT; no 3D motion synthesis, no learned compatibility network, no reward critic or judge in the generation loop, no RSI, no performance claims, no dataset counts or internal filenames. Do not claim SFT and MOSS are combined in the same run. Model names must be spelled exactly as specified. Preserve the feedback loop, not a simple left-to-right pipeline. Keep the visual readable when scaled to a full-width two-column paper figure.
